statement: The 2004 abstract states: compartment model with lispro s.c. absorption and gut absorption submodels; Bayesian parameter estimation of time-varying model parameters; moving target trajectory giving slow normalization of elevated and faster normalization of low glucose; 15 clinical experiments with IV glucose sampling and pump changes every 15 min; quoted verbatim: "mean square error proportionally related to the prediction horizon with the value of 0.2 mmol L(-1) per 15 min" (the printed unit is not that of a mean square error, so the metric is ambiguous and is not used as an accuracy figure); Clarke error grid 95% zone A / 5% zone B up to 60 min (n = 1674); fasting/overnight scope.

The 2004 physiological parameter table, however, IS restated in open sources (SRC-PUB-MATH-REVIEW-0001; consistent with SRC-PUB-MATH-0008 after the EGP0 correction), so the physiology is not blocked on the closed original.

statement: Wilinska 2010 gives the s.c. insulin submodel as three compartments (two s.c. depots and plasma) with identical transfer rate k_a and elimination k_e.
locator: Submodel of Subcutaneous Insulin Absorption; Appendix

statement: Wilinska 2010's plasma-insulin equation renders in MathML as dl/dt = k_a S2(t)/V_1 - k_e I(t); the fraction is present, and only the symbols are misprinted (l for I, V_1 for V_I). The dimensionally consistent form dI/dt = k_a S2/V_I - k_e I (k_a = 1/t_maxI) is also printed by Reenberg (1c), Rashid (A-1) and implied by Freil.
Pompa Table 3 lists for its single 70 kg Hovorka virtual subject: tau_S = 55 min, k_e = 0.138 1/min, V_I = 0.12*BW L (eq 182), u_basal = 6.68 mU/min (= 0.40 U/h).

Paoletti/Jacobs use a dual-channel s.c. insulin model with Michaelis-Menten local degradation (Wilinska 2005) and give K = 0.7958, k_ia1 = 0.0113, k_ia2 = 0.0197, k_e = 0.1735, V_maxLD = 2.9639 mU/min, k_mLD = 47.5305 mU.
Insulin action is three first-order remote effects x1 (transport/distribution), x2 (disposal), x3 (EGP) driven by plasma insulin.

Notation variant plus internal inconsistency in Wilinska 2010: the appendix prints dx_i/dt = -k_ai x_i + S_i k_bi I with text 'S_IT = k_a1/k_b1', while Table 1 lists 'k_b1..3' as activation rates in min^-1 (0.0034, 0.056, 0.024), of the same magnitude as the deactivation rates k_a1..3 of Pompa/Freil (0.006, 0.06, 0.03). Two dimensionally consistent equivalent parameterizations exist: dx_i/dt = -k_ai x_i + k_bi I with S_i = k_bi/k_ai (Pompa, Reenberg, Freil, Rashid), or dx_i/dt = k_i(-x_i + S_i I) with one rate k_i in min^-1 (Paoletti eq 19). The printed Wilinska form is steady-state consistent with x_i = S_i I only if the same rate appears in both terms; INFERENCE: read Wilinska's tabulated rates as k_i in the Paoletti form.
premises: k_b has units L/(mU min^2) in Pompa

statement: Wilinska 2010 MathML prints EGP = EGP0[1 + x3(t)] (if EGP >= 0, else 0). Pompa (165), Paoletti (15), Reenberg (7a), Freil (7)/(10) and Rashid (A-5) all print EGP0(1 - x3), and x3 is described as the insulin effect on (suppression of) EGP. INFERENCE: EGP = EGP0(1 - x3) is the intended form; the '+' is a typographical error.

statement: Pompa eq (183) EGP0 = 0.161*BoW mmol/min is a dropped-zero misprint of 0.0161*BoW mmol/min (16.1 umol kg^-1 min^-1). Evidence: (i) with Pompa's own Table 3 values the basal steady state at G0 = 5 mmol/L and u_basal = 6.68 mU/min balances (|dQ1/dt| < 1e-4 mmol/min) only with 0.0161; with 0.161 glucose would rise at about 38 mmol/L per hour at the stated 'starting value' (CHK-01); (ii) an independent open restatement of the Hovorka 2004 parameters gives EGP0 = 0.0161*BW mmol/min and F01 = 0.0097*BW (SRC-PUB-MATH-REVIEW-0001); (iii) Wilinska Table 1 population mean 16.9 umol kg^-1 min^-1 and Paoletti 0.0158*BW are of the same order.

statement: Two public variants of insulin-independent flux exist: piecewise F01*min(G/4.5,1) with renal 0.003(G-9)V_G (Pompa/Reenberg), and Michaelis-Menten F01s G/(G+1) with F01s = F01/0.85 and sampled renal parameters (Wilinska 2010 simulator).

Gut absorption is a two-compartment chain with bioavailability (A_G/Bio) and shared time constant t_maxG. Wilinska 2010 adds a ceiling: if U_G > U_Gceil then t_max := t_max_ceil = G2/U_Gceil, with U_Gceil drawn from U[0.02, 0.035] mmol kg^-1 min^-1 (printed 'mmol/kg^-1 min^-1'). The ceiling is a per-kg RATE; the total-flux ceiling is U_Gceil*BW mmol/min (Paoletti: 0.0275*BW mmol/min, the midpoint). Inputs differ: Wilinska D(t) is an amount ingested at time t (impulse into G1, scaled by Bio), Pompa d(t) is a rate in g/min.

Interstitial glucose follows dC/dt = k_a_int (G - C). In Paoletti the CGM output is C plus Gaussian noise of variance 0.1521 mmol^2/L^2 (SD 0.39 mmol/L, described as 5% of the 7.8 mmol/L glucose value), with k_a_int = 0.025 1/min for that subject.

Paoletti initialise the Hovorka-type model by solving for x(0) and basal insulin such that dx/dt = 0 at 7.8 mmol/L without meals, and screen feasibility (>300 mg/dL with no insulin; <100 mg/dL at 15 U/h).

The Cambridge controller is initialised from user-supplied quantities: weight, total daily insulin dose and basal insulin (2009-2011; 2018 v0.3.46 downloads pre-programmed basal and enters weight and TDI; 2021 HX v0.3.71 text names weight and TDI). Wilinska 2009 states these feed estimates of insulin sensitivity and glucose/insulin distribution volumes. The mapping is not public.
Cambridge control cycle: 15 min (2004, 2009-2011), 10 min (v0.3.46, 2018), 8-12 min (CamAPS HX v0.3.71).

Cambridge MPC (v0.02.02) updates two model quantities from sensor glucose with a Kalman filter approach - a glucose flux quantifying model misspecification and CHO bioavailability - and combines several parallel competing models (different s.c. insulin absorption/action and CHO absorption) by a stochastic approach.
Algorithm v0.3.46 added 'enhanced adaptation of insulin needs based on analysis of past performance and identification of the time of day when insulin needs are consistently lower or higher'.

Cambridge MPC (2009-2011 versions) forecast plasma glucose over 2.5 h; targets 104 mg/dL minimum elevated up to 132 mg/dL (2009) or 5.8-7.3 mmol/L depending on fasting/postprandial status and prediction accuracy (2011, 2017, 2018). CamAPS HX v0.3.71: nominal 5.8 mmol/L adjustable 4.4-11.0 mmol/L. The horizon of current commercial versions is not public.

Published historical Cambridge safety checks: max infusion 2-5x basal depending on SG/time since meal/CHO; shut-off at 77 mg/dL (2009) or <= 4.3 mmol/L (2011, 2017); reduction on rapid fall; basal cap on inferred occlusion.
Cambridge trials state the algorithm was intentionally detuned for safety in a 2013 multicentre comparison.

Conditional INFERENCE: if a physiological predictor's states are propagated from the complete DELIVERED insulin history, each delivered unit enters S1 exactly once and its modelled future glucose effect is already in the predicted trajectory; under that premise, adding or subtracting a separate IOB-derived glucose effect in the prediction would count the same insulin twice. The rule depends on the predictor's accounting (complete history, which insulin is inside the model). It does not forbid an independent exposure/safety supervisor that limits or reduces commands; whether and how such a supervisor exists is implementer-owned.

statement: With CGM-only output and unannounced meals, meal appearance and a glucose-flux correction are not separately identifiable over short windows (both enter dQ1/dt additively); only their sum is.

Cambridge simulator intra-subject variability: sinusoidal oscillations of 5% amplitude and 3 h period on selected parameters, phase drawn from U[0, 3 h]; Bio and t_max subject to additional 20% inter-occasion variability. Aspart plasma-insulin time-to-peak (PK) in pump users: inter-subject CV 33%, intra-subject CV 27%.

The cited public scientific literature supplies physiological foundation mathematics, generic MPC and verbal adaptation descriptions. It does not supply a complete commercial controller specification; independent controller design is required.

statement: CamAPS FX is described by Cambridge authors as 'Treat to target adaptive MPC (Cambridge algorithm)'.
Copp et al. model: Ts = 5 min, u = insulin per sample minus basal per sample [U], y = BG - 110 mg/dL.
Transfer function (1800 g/u_TDI) z^-3/((1-p1 z^-1)(1-p2 z^-1)^2), p1 = 0.98, p2 = 0.965, g = -90(1-p1)(1-p2)^2, from van Heusden et al. 2012.

State-space realization with D = -B/10, C = [0 0 1]; positive disturbance raises modeled BG 'akin to the consumption of carbohydrates'; d = 0.5 counteracts 0.05 U.

Copp eq (7) literally writes c(C x_k); C x_k is the deviation from y_s = 110 mg/dL. The rendered Fig. 1(b) plots c over 40-240 mg/dL with c(40) about 2.5, minimum near 100-120 and c(240) about 1.9; arithmetic gives c(40) = 2.52, c(240) = 1.89, argmin about 105.5 mg/dL when the argument is ABSOLUTE glucose, whereas c(0) = 5.03 (maximal cost at 110 mg/dL) under the deviation reading. statement: The asymmetry ratio stated is 4^2 = 16 (lam_lo/lam_hi = 0.02/0.005 squared); text extraction shows '42'.

U := {0 <= u_t + u_BASAL Ts/(60 min/h) <= u_MAX} with u_MAX = 25 U described as 'the maximum bolus size the CSII pump is allowed to command ... so large it will not be met during normal operation ... included to safeguard against data problems'; D = {0 <= d <= 0.5}; no constraint on measurement noise; the set X for x_{t-L} is not specified for the glucose instance.
Because d >= 0, the MHE cannot attribute unexpected glucose falls to the disturbance; such falls are absorbed by the initial-state and noise variables.

Min-max cost (7): sum_{k=t+1}^{t+T} c(.)^2 + sum_{k=t}^{t+M-1} lam_u u_k^2 - sum_{k=t-L}^{t+T-1} lam_d d_k^2 - sum_{k=t-L}^{t} lam_n n_k^2, T = 9, M = 5, L = 3 (T, M as in [17]; L by experimentation), lam_u = 2, lam_d = 2, lam_n = 300; u_k = 0 (basal) for k in [t+M, t+T-1]; re-solved every Ts = 5 min. Argument of c per CLM-PUB-MATH-0044.
The paper omits meal announcement, IOB constraints, diurnal zones/constraints and other clinical safety features and states its simulation results are not representative of expected trial results.

Evaluation used the commercially licensed 10-subject UVA/Padova simulator, 110 simulations, three unannounced 90 g meals, 28 h with 2 h open loop; no formal stability proof for the glucose application.

Published command mapping: first element u*_t; the absolute command is floored to the 0.05 U pump resolution and the floored-away remainder is carried to the next sample (Gondhalekar sec 2.7 carry-over, defined on commanded amounts). Gondhalekar notes upper bounds are enforced on the MPC solution before discretization, so an active bound is temporarily violated and met only on average.

Arithmetic INFERENCE (not a source-confirmed bug): with Gondhalekar eq (2) A, C and eq (3b) Q = I3, R = 1000, P iterated to convergence (58 iterations), the printed gain L^T = -(R+CPC^T)^-1 CPA^T used in the printed filter form x_i = x^_i + L(y - y^_i), x^_i = A x_{i-1} + B u_{i-1} gives error dynamics (I - LC)A with spectral radius 2.24 (2.03 if used in predictor form). The standard predictor gain K = A P C^T/(R + CPC^T) in Copp's predictor form (10) gives A - KC with radius 0.80; the standard filter gain P C^T/(R + CPC^T) gives (I - KC)A with radius 0.80. Copp eq (10) states K is 'designed as in [17]'.

statement: MPC/LO comparator: asymmetric input weights R^ = 7000, R~ = 100, zone [80,140] mg/dL, Ny = 9, Nu = 5; formulated as a strictly convex QP.

Gondhalekar's clinical version adds: diurnal zone [80,140] mg/dL by day and [110,170] mg/dL by night with cosine transitions (tau = 4, 6, 22, 24 h after midnight); input bound u_bar = u_MAX for t in [tau1, tau3] and beta*u_BASAL*T/60 (beta = 1.8) otherwise; an IOB upper bound from 8 h histories with 2/4/6/8 h curves selected by CGM; and an announced-meal bolus rule.
The IOB decay curves theta_l are given only graphically: 'no mathematical definition is available'.

In Basis B, only u_{t-3..t-1} enter the estimation explicitly; older insulin acts through the estimated x_{t-L}. An IOB upper bound added from a separate 8-h history therefore represents the same insulin a second time (as a constraint, not as predicted glucose effect) and must be tuned/tested for over-conservatism.
Saddle-point existence is assumed (Assumption 1); for linear systems with quadratic costs, observability plus sufficiently large lam_n, lam_d suffice (ACC 2016 Thm 2, Cor. 1).

The authors solve the min-max with a primal-dual interior-point method (Copp & Hespanha 2017; dissertation Algorithms 4.3.1/4.4.2) and state the 5-min sample period exceeds computation by orders of magnitude; for nonconvex cases they suggest multiple random initializations.
MPC/MHE can include uncertain parameters theta in Theta as additional maximization variables; the glucose paper lists parameter learning only as future work.

simglucose (MIT license, commit a6f67775...) implements the UVA/Padova 2008 model for research purposes with 30 virtual patients (10 adolescents, adults, children), sensor models (Dexcom, GuardianRT, Navigator) and pump models (Cozmo, Insulet, 0.05 U increments).
The simglucose maintainer states the virtual patient parameters came from the 2008 UVa/Padova academic Matlab version obtainable from the T1DMS distributor.

simglucose's MIT license covers its code; the provenance/licensing of the embedded UVA/Padova S2008 parameter cohort is a separate question not resolved by the MIT license, and simglucose is not the FDA-accepted commercial simulator nor clinical validation.

statement: S2008 T1D parameter distributions were derived from non-diabetic adult distributions; S2013 updated them.
ReplayBG (GPL-3.0, licence file COPYING.md) identifies personalised digital twins from CGM/insulin/meal data supplied in a prescribed CSV format, with body weight and basal (u2ss) as patient info.

The Cambridge simulator (Wilinska 2010) has 18 virtual subjects; its equations and population distributions are public in the paper, but its software and individual parameter sets are not published there.
Using a Hovorka-equation plant to evaluate a Hovorka-model controller is not structurally independent; simglucose (UVA/Padova structure) is structurally different from both bases.

Freil et al. (2024) Table 1 restates the Hovorka 2004 parameters for BW = 70 kg: EGP0 = 0.0161*BW mmol/min, F01 = 0.0097*BW mmol/min, k12 = 0.066, k_a1..3 = 0.006/0.06/0.03 1/min, V_G = 0.16*BW L, k_b1 = 3.07e-5, k_b2 = 4.92e-5, k_b3 = 0.0016, V_I = 0.120*BW L, tau_S = 55 min, k_e = 0.138 1/min, and uses EGP = EGP0(1 - x3).

Pompa Table 3 internal consistency: at G0 = 5 mmol/L, u_basal = 6.68 mU/min, BW = 70 kg, the basal steady state balances with EGP0 = 0.0161*BW (dQ1/dt = -0.0001 mmol/min) and not with the printed 0.161*BW (dQ1/dt = +7.10 mmol/min, about +38 mmol/L per hour).

At retrieval (2026-10-07) neither Crossref (no update-to/updated-by relation) nor Europe PMC (no correction entry) records a correction for Pompa 2021, Wilinska 2010, Gondhalekar 2016, Copp 2018 or Wilinska 2009; all errata resolutions in this basis are therefore inferences, not publisher-confirmed errata.

Arithmetic diagnostic (CHK-02; not an observation): in the 2004-lineage model with Pompa Table 3 values, unit bolus into S1, Euler integration, the insulin mass in S1+S2+V_I*I is 39%, 7.6% and 0.2% of the bolus at 2 h, 4 h and 8 h, while the remaining share of the x1 (transport/distribution) effect integral is 84%, 50% and 13%. Insulin compartment mass is therefore not remaining action. The x1 share covers one channel only; x2 and x3 were not evaluated in CHK-02, and x1 acts multiplied by Q1, so it is not the whole glucose-lowering action and not a clinical or AAPS IOB. History length is implementer-owned and should be chosen against the action time scale of the chosen model, not absorption alone.

Initialising a physiological or Basis-B state at basal steady state assumes no insulin beyond basal was delivered within the action time scale. If prior boluses or temporary rates are unknown (first start, lost history, reinstall), that assumption is unverifiable from CGM over short windows because recent insulin, meals and sensitivity act through the same output. Design options include retained delivery history, or explicit initial-state uncertainty with no above-basal insulin until the history covers the action time scale. Either option only avoids adding insulin on an unverified assumption; neither is a safety guarantee, because already-delivered unknown insulin and basal delivery itself can still cause harm. Residual risk belongs to implementer-owned hazard analysis.

statement: Dimensional reading of Copp eqs (4)-(7): with y in mg/dL, the constant 0.1 has units (mg/dL)^-1 and 10, 20, r_lo, r_hi have units mg/dL, so h(y) is in mg/dL; lam_lo, lam_hi (0.02, 0.005) then carry units (mg/dL)^-1 to make c dimensionless. lam_u = 2 carries U^-2 (u in U per sample), lam_d = 2 carries U^-2 (d enters through D = -B/10, i.e. U-equivalent per sample), lam_n = 300 carries (mg/dL)^-2. The weights are not universally dimensionless: a change of glucose unit (mmol/L), sample period or insulin unit requires rescaling every constant to preserve the published problem.

Sampled numerical diagnostic, not a proof or certification: for the published glucose instance (X = R^3, D = [0, 0.5]^12, U compact by (5), all L+1 = 4 window samples present, published weights), J is convex in u if c^2 is convex (c >= 0 and convex on the CHK-04 grid, numerically), composed with outputs affine in u; and a Hessian upper bound in (x_{t-L}, d) built from the grid-sampled maximum curvature of c^2 (CHK-04) is negative definite at the evaluated u_TDI points (CHK-05). If that curvature bound held globally, compact U, continuity and Sion's theorem would give min-max = max-min with an attained inner maximum, i.e. a saddle point. Global validity of the bound is not established, so saddle-point existence is NOT established; the evaluated u_TDI points are not thresholds of any kind. With 2 or fewer of the 4 window samples (CHK-09 subsets at u_TDI = 40) the bound is positive: only the sampled guarantee is lost; whether concavity is actually lost or the inner maximum becomes unbounded is HOLD (not established). Runtime duality-gap checks remain required.

For the source carry-over scheme with resolution delta: 0 <= carry < delta, and the quantized command can exceed a pre-quantization bound by less than one increment per sample (CHK-07). The source meets active bounds only on average; that is source behaviour, not adopted. A platform limit must hold on every quantized command (no average-bound waiver). Any rounding residual must not authorize make-up insulin across cycles, suspensions, or failed, partial or uncertain deliveries; discarding the residual complies. Delivery recording and reconciliation stay with the app, not with a controller carry rule.
locator: Sec 2.7 and its remark on temporary violation; CHK-07

statement: Gut-ceiling units: Wilinska's U_Gceil is per kg (mmol kg^-1 min^-1); a total-flux comparison with U_G (mmol/min) requires multiplication by BW (Paoletti's 0.0275*BW mmol/min equals the U[0.02,0.035] midpoint). The ceiling is applied by lengthening t_max so that U_G = U_Gceil, a rate cap that conserves absorbed mass.

Wilinska 2010 Table 2 distributions are historical virtual-population sampling distributions: the printed Gaussian R_cl ~ N(0.01, 0.025^2) puts 34% probability on negative clearance (k_a, k_e about 3e-5), with no stated truncation; reading the printed 'exp(p) ~ N(m, s^2)' as ln p ~ N gives medians V_G = 0.15 L/kg, t_maxG = 40.0 min (equal to Pompa's 40 min), k_a_int = 0.093 1/min. They are not startup values, parameter defaults or safe bounds.

Gondhalekar's diurnal zone and night input bound are functions of local clock time in hours after midnight; the source gives no rule for time zones, DST changes, travel or clock corrections. Time-of-day dependence requires an implementer-defined, tested time base.
Copp et al. eq (10) states the MPC/LO observer in predictor form x^_{t+1} = A x^_t + K(y_t - y^_t) + B u_t, y^_t = C x^_t, with 'the gain K designed as in [17]' (Gondhalekar 2016).

Basis-B gain and delay units: steady-state gain -162000/u_TDI (mg/dL) per (U/sample sustained) = -13500/u_TDI (mg/dL) per (U/h sustained); a deviation input at sample t first changes the output at sample t+3 (15 min); with u_TDI = 40 U a 1 U impulse reaches its minimum -31.2 mg/dL 69 samples (345 min) after the input sample; pole time constants 247 min and 140 min (double).

Copp eq (5)'s u_MAX = 25 U and Gondhalekar's u_MAX bound are published simulation/data-guard constants. They do not define, and must not be imported as, a therapy limit; whether a bound is 'never reached' in simulation says nothing about its safety in use.

claim: oref1 is not a separate codebase: SMB and UAM are branches inside the same lib/determine-basal/determine-basal.js as oref0 temp-basal logic. SMB is enabled only if the caller passes microBolusAllowed=true AND one profile enable condition holds (enableSMB_always / _with_COB / _after_carbs / _with_temptarget(<100 mg/dL) / _high_bg); a high temp target (>100 mg/dL) disables it unless allowSMB_with_high_temptarget. The oref0 CLI additionally forces microbolus off unless an ./autotune directory exists.

claim: determine_basal is a per-call function with no persistent state of its own. Every time-dependent decision is computed from inputs: CGM age from glucose_status.date vs currentTime, SMB spacing from iob_data[0].lastBolusTime, temp reconciliation from iob_data[0].lastTemp (oref0 only), carb timing from meal_data.lastCarbTime. In oref0, lastBolusTime and lastTemp come from pump history (lib/iob/index.js). In AAPS, the SMB-spacing input is iob_data.lastBolusTime of iobArray[0] (DetermineBasalSMB.kt L277, L1098), which IobCobCalculatorPlugin sets from the newest valid bolus with amount > 0 within the IOB range (L524-532); MealData.lastBolusTime (newest DB bolus, L374-376) is a separate field. currentTime is injectable in both ports, and that injectability is what makes deterministic replay possible.

claim: In OpenAPS rigs, the work of handling insulin-delivery uncertainty sits in bin/oref0-pump-loop.sh, not in determine-basal. Before an SMB the loop: (a) refreshes pump history and requires it to be under 5 min old; (b) requires the pump clock within 90 s of system time, resetting it if more than 55 s off; (c) re-runs IOB and determine-basal after reading the current temp; (d) enacts the temp before the bolus and verifies it (rate within ±0.03 U/h, duration window -5/+20 min); (e) checks the pump status is normal, not bolusing and not suspended; (f) requires the reservoir to have dropped by between 0 and 0.1 U, both against the previous reading and against the reservoir value embedded in the suggestion; (g) requires deliverAt within ±60 s and a fresh suggestion file; (h) retries steps up to 3 times, and retries a failed bolus once only after redoing every check; (i) refreshes pump history after any enact or bolus.

claim: In AAPS, the algorithm does not decide failed-SMB fallback; it consumes a boolean. When the SMB command callback reports neither success nor enacted, LoopPlugin re-invokes the loop after 1000 ms with tempBasalFallback=true. OpenAPSSMBPlugin sets microBolusAllowed = isSMBModeEnabled(Constraint(!tempBasalFallback)). With microBolusAllowed false, enable_smb returns false and the run takes the temp-basal-only path. SafetyPlugin also forces SMB off whenever closed loop is not allowed.
envelope: AAPS master at pinned SHA. No algorithm output signals 'SMB failed'. The only algorithm-side SMB eligibility signals are internal (minGuardBG, maxDelta, bg>threshold, interval). Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: AAPS guards SMB admission in several places outside the algorithm. (1) LoopPlugin zeroes the SMB if the newest DB bolus is within ApsMaxSmbFrequency minutes (L507-512). (2) It calls applyTBRRequest first and requests the SMB only if the TBR callback reports enacted or success, setting deliverAt to that time (L619-656). 'Success' includes non-enacting outcomes: no TBR requested ('nochangerequested', L765-767), a cancel or base-basal-equivalent request when no temp is active ('basal set correctly', L783-794), and an equivalent active temp left running ('let temp basal run', L832-844). An SMB can therefore proceed with no new temp and without any zero or low temp, and an enacted/success report is the driver/queue result, not independent confirmation of physical delivery. (3) applySMBRequest re-checks the interval, pump initialisation and suspension (L860-881). (4) CommandQueue.bolus rejects an SMB if any bolus is queued or running, or if a bolus newer than lastKnownBolusTime exists, then applies bolus constraints (L269-281, L317-338). (5) CommandSMBBolus re-checks the interval at execution time and drops the SMB as 'too old' if more than 1 min has passed since deliverAtTheLatest (L42-58). Upstream unit tests cover the two queue rejections.

claim: Neither port verifies insulin delivery inside the algorithm. determine-basal trusts iob_data fully and checks only that it exists and has iob and activity fields. In oref0, IOB comes from pump-history parsing: it drops future boluses and duplicate or out-of-order records, splits temps around suspends, turns net temp basal into ±0.05 U pseudo-boluses, and adds a synthetic temp starting 1 min in the future (zero for 240 min in the iobWithZeroTemp array). In AAPS, IOB comes from database records with isValid=true. The PumpSync contract counts a temporary-id bolus toward IOB from creation until synced, and it stays counted even if never synced.
envelope: Driver correctness is assumed, not verified. If a driver drops a delivered bolus, every layer under-counts IOB. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: CGM validity handling (mg/dL, minutes). oref0 treats bg <= 10, bg == 38, noise >= 3, BG age > 12 min or < -5 min, or 'too flat' as unusable. Too flat means bg > 60, delta == 0 and short_avgdelta and long_avgdelta both strictly between -1 and 1, unless device == 'fakecgm'. When data is unusable it issues no increase: a running temp above profile basal is replaced by a 30-min temp at profile basal, a zero temp longer than 30 min is shortened to 30 min, otherwise it returns without a rate. For stale or future-dated data with lastTempAge < 10 min it returns without a rate at all (L206-208), so any running temp, including a recently set high temp, continues. Noise >= 2 raises targets by max(1.1, noisyCGMTargetMultiplier), capped at 200. In AAPS, getGlucoseStatusData returns null if the newest bucket is more than 7 min old; OpenAPSSMBPlugin.invoke then returns with no APS result (L306, L319-323) and LoopPlugin.invoke returns without issuing a command (L477-487). On that path the algorithm's own >12-min stale branch (which replaces a high temp with profile basal) is never reached, so a running high temp continues until it expires. AAPS noise is hard-coded 0, FLAT is flagged only for Libre1 over 45 min, and doubled readings force maxIOB to 0.
envelope: Numeric values are version facts for these pins, not recommendations. Tested in oref0: bg<=10 cases and 'BG data is too old'. Stale-with-lastTempAge<10 and flat-CGM have no unit test in determine-basal.test.js. Only the LoopPlugin.invoke path was read for stale-data handling; other app components were not inspected. Temp expiry is a pump/driver property not verified in these sources. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: Low-glucose protection: threshold = min_bg - 0.5*(min_bg - 40) mg/dL (L340). AAPS raises it to lgsThreshold if that is higher. If bg < threshold or minGuardBG < threshold, a zero temp of 30-120 min (rounded to 30) is returned (L923-931). The exception is bg < threshold while IOB < -20 min of basal and BG is rising faster than expected (L919-921), in which case evaluation continues. SMB is disabled when minGuardBG < threshold and is only considered when bg > threshold. minGuardBG is not the minimum of a single blended trajectory: it is built from per-trajectory minimum guard values (no initial wait), blending minCOBGuardBG and minUAMGuardBG by fractionCarbsLeft when carbs are modelled and UAM is on, otherwise using minCOBGuardBG, minUAMGuardBG or minIOBGuardBG (L739-751). Upstream unit tests assert zero or low temps in low scenarios.
envelope: Formula and constants are oref0 design choices. A new controller needs its own justified low-protection rule, not this exact formula. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: Bounds and rounding. A rate passed through setTempBasal is clamped to [0, maxSafeBasal], where maxSafeBasal = min(max_basal, max_daily_safety_multiplier (default 3) * max_daily_basal, current_basal_safety_multiplier (default 4) * current_basal) U/h; this is unit-tested. In the high-temp branch, insulinReq (U) is capped at max_iob - iob at decision time, and the 30-min rate is basal + 2*insulinReq U/h, i.e. insulinReq units above basal over 30 min (L1069-1077). The cap applies to that single decision-time quantity; it is not applied to a combined bolus-plus-temp result (CLM-PUB-OREF-0011). If iob > max_iob, a temp at the sensitivity-adjusted basal is set, or a running temp at about that rate is left running (L1056-1064). In oref0 the IOB compared with max_iob is net of scheduled basal: temps become +/-0.05 U pseudo-boluses relative to the (sensitivity-adjusted) scheduled rate (history.js L548-564) and are summed with bolus IOB (total.js L67-92); the code comment at L237 still calls max_iob 'non-bolus IOB'. Documented max_iob meaning differs by version and mode: oref0 >= 0.6.0 documents all-source IOB (basal and bolus); AAPS documents total IOB in SMB mode and basal IOB in AMA. The oref0 profile default is max_iob = 0. oref0 rounds rates per pump model (0.025/0.05/0.1 U/h). The AAPS Kotlin round_basal is the identity function: rate rounding (tempAbsoluteStep), pump max TBR, hard-limit max basal, max bolus (preference and hard limit), bolus-step rounding, max IOB (preference and hard limit) and LGS-mode max IOB are applied by platform constraint plugins, several of them unit-tested.
envelope: Multiplier defaults are version facts. AAPS basal-IOB internals were not inspected; the net-of-scheduled-basal statement is verified for oref0 only. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: SMB sizing and gates (units U, U/h, min). microBolus = floor(min(insulinReq/2, maxBolus) / bolus_increment) * bolus_increment. maxBolus = current_basal * maxSMBBasalMinutes/60, or * maxUAMSMBBasalMinutes/60 when IOB > COB/CR and IOB > 0, rounded to 0.1 (30 min of basal when the setting is undefined). The SMB interval defaults to 3 min, clamped to 1-10. maxDelta > 20% of BG disables SMB (oref0 allows a configurable value capped at 30%; AAPS fixes it at 20%). A low or zero temp is returned with the SMB only when the worst-case durationReq is > 0: a zero temp of 30-60 min, or a 30-min low temp when durationReq < 30 min (L1112-1133, L1165-1169). When insulinReq > 0 but the microbolus rounds below one increment, durationReq is forced to 0 and no SMB is set (L1118-1120). When durationReq <= 0 with a non-zero microbolus, no low temp is returned; execution falls through (L1164-1171) to the high-temp code (L1173-1198) with rT.units still set. By static reading, one result can therefore carry an SMB plus a 30-min temp above basal (or a running temp left in place), both sized from the same max_iob-capped insulinReq. The AAPS port has the same structure (DetermineBasalSMB.kt L1070-1153). AAPS measures the interval in seconds with a 6 s tolerance. No call in oref0 tests/determine-basal.test.js passes any argument after tempBasalFunctions, so microBolusAllowed is always undefined there and the SMB path has no oref0 unit test.

claim: Documentation is not the same as code requirements. The oref1 doc says SMB is disabled when basal < 0.3 U/h; no such check was found in the listed pinned oref0 files (SRC-PUB-OREF-0002, SRC-PUB-OREF-0003); the rest of the pinned tree was not checked. The doc 'requires' autotune, but code enforces this only by checking that an ./autotune directory exists. The doc gives a 60 s pump-clock tolerance, while the code resets above 55 s and fails at 90 s or more. In AAPS, user-side gating (objectives: open loop -> LGS with maxIOB 0 -> closed loop -> SMB) is documented; LGS maxIOB = 0 is code-enforced in LoopPlugin.applyMaxIOBConstraints (L417-425); enforcement of the objectives themselves was not inspected.
envelope: Absence finding covers only the listed pinned files; re-check the full pinned tree before relying on it. The check may exist in older releases. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: Guard-order defect at the pin, by static source reading only. Two upstream test cases in tests/determine-basal.test.js call determine_basal with iob_data and currenttemp undefined: 'profile should contain min_bg,max_bg' (L465-468, asserting the target_bg error) and 'iob_data should not be undefined' (L470-473, asserting the iob_data error). In pinned determine-basal.js, L188 reads iob_data.lastTemp before the target_bg guard (L253-258) and before the iob_data guard (L361-364). Reading a property of undefined throws in JavaScript, so neither case can reach the error return its test asserts. In bin/oref0-pump-loop.sh, calculate_iob copies a new iob.json only if it is non-empty and has .[0].iob; otherwise that loop iteration does not proceed to determine-basal (L644-652).
envelope: Static reading of the pinned files only. No test execution outcome is asserted and no commit is identified as the origin of the defect. Practical lesson: the upstream tests express a graceful missing-input requirement that the pinned guard order cannot satisfy, so a new controller should test missing-input handling directly.

claim: Outputs are bounded in time. Temps are normally 30 min, LGS zero temps 30-120 min, SMB-paired low temps up to 60 min. oref0-pump-loop accepts a suggestion only if deliverAt is within 60 s, and AAPS drops an SMB more than 1 min past its deliverAt. When inputs are missing (no profile, no glucose status, autosens unavailable, pump queue busy for 2 min, base basal not loaded), AAPS returns without issuing any new command. Any temp already running, including one above basal, therefore continues for its remaining programmed duration, and delivery reverts to scheduled basal only when that temp expires on the pump. 'No command' is therefore not by itself a safe outcome. oref0 returns rT.error, which the wrapper prints to stderr instead of a suggestion on stdout and the loop treats as a failure; in the inspected paths no temp is enacted from an error result, so a running temp likewise continues.
envelope: Reversion to scheduled basal relies on the pump enforcing temp expiry, a pump/driver property not verified in these sources. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: Reason output and replay. rT.reason is a free-text string summarising COB, Dev, BGI, ISF, CR, minPredBG, minGuardBG, IOBpredBG/COBpredBG/UAMpredBG and the branch taken. AAPS persists each APS result (insertOrUpdateApsResult) along with its inputs (glucoseStatus, iobData, profile, mealData, currentTemp, inputConstraints). AAPS's ReplayApsResultsTest compares JS and Kotlin numeric fields (rate, duration, units, eventualBG, insulinReq, IOB, COB, ...) on archived cases. It leaves the reason-equality assertion commented out and skips cases with whole-number delta because the implementations differ there.
envelope: The reason text is a diagnostic convention, not a tested contract. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.

claim: A new insulin-only controller that runs as an AAPS APS plugin through LoopPlugin and CommandQueue (at the upstream pin) would inherit: driver-reported enact/success results and PumpSync history recording (temp-id before delivery or history read after delivery, depending on the driver), queue serialisation and SMB rejection rules, a 3-layer SMB interval check, 1-min SMB expiry, hard limits and pump rounding, closed-loop and LGS gating (objective enforcement not inspected), suspend handling, TBR-before-SMB ordering (with the CLM-PUB-OREF-0006 caveat that a non-enacting TBR 'success' lets the SMB proceed without a new temp), and the failed-SMB -> temp-only re-invocation, which is a fresh recomputation with SMB disabled, not a retry of the same bolus. It would NOT inherit what OpenAPSSMBPlugin.invoke does for itself: profile DIA/IC/ISF/basal hard-limit checks, returning when autosens or glucose is unavailable, building the max_iob and max_basal inputs from constraints, and mapping tempBasalFallback to the SMB-disable input. The new plugin must reproduce or deliberately replace these. Pump-command retries already live in the queue/driver layer.

claim: Exact numerical equivalence with Oref is not a meaningful acceptance criterion, even within the AAPS project. The AAPS Kotlin port knowingly differs from the oref0 JS: SMB interval in seconds with 6 s tolerance, fixed 20% maxDelta, no high-BG/A52 SMB rules, identity round_basal, noise hard-coded to 0, flat detection moved to a plugin, the lastTemp reconciliation removed, and dynamic-ISF branches added. Its replay test excludes whole-number-delta cases and does not compare reason text. The benchmark is therefore behavioural, not numerical: properties such as 'no new insulin increase on stale CGM, with stated treatment of running temps'. Such properties are benchmarks for a specification to state and test; they do not describe a composed outcome that Oref or AAPS guarantees (see CLM-PUB-OREF-0008, CLM-PUB-OREF-0015).

claim: Oref's own engineering bar before code reached users was: unit tests asserting direction and bounds (mostly 'rate == 0', 'duration > 29', 'rate below X', clamps), a few shell-level CLI tests, and documented staged user rollout (oref0 for 2+ weeks before oref1; AAPS objectives). The oref0 SMB path has no unit test, and by static reading two determine-basal test cases cannot reach their assertions at the pin (CLM-PUB-OREF-0013). There is no evidence in these sources of formal verification, regulatory clearance, fixed simulator acceptance, or measured device energy as a precondition for algorithm work. So a research spec for a new controller cannot reasonably be required to carry those, while implementation PRs can be held to property-level unit tests and integration tests. This does not lower the project requirement stated in SPEC.md: changed dosing behaviour and relevant failure paths must be verified in simulation or replay before an implementation is considered ready, and passing tests or simulations is not clinical validation. Oref clinical or field experience does not transfer as safety evidence for a different controller.
envelope: Absence of evidence is limited to the inspected files and pages. Upstream may have process material elsewhere (e.g. papers) that was not inspected. The project-requirement sentence refers to SPEC.md, not to a public source.

claim: Restart and replay. A controller that, like determine-basal, derives SMB spacing and temp state from persisted history rather than in-memory counters is restart-safe in the sense that a process restart cannot reset its spacing or IOB, provided the platform records each bolus at or before delivery (PumpSync temp-id path) and the AAPS layers re-check the newest DB bolus. PumpSync also documents drivers that add boluses only after reading pump history (syncBolusWithPumpId); for those, a delivered bolus can be absent from the DB for a window, and spacing derived from history is only as current as that history. Any controller state that does not live in AAPS history (filters, estimators, integrators) is NOT covered by this inheritance. Its restart behaviour must be specified and tested by the implementer.
envelope: Does not cover driver-level loss of history. Fact about nightscout/AndroidAPS@598e2eb39c7e15876e4c42876a2162bffcb4fe5f (upstream pin); applicability to this fork's HEAD not verified.
